topPRs.title: feat: enforce review period delay ranges and lockbox consistency
topPRs.author: 0xarktos
topPRs.body:
## Description

Adds validation for the per-chain review period delays (proof maturity, dispute game finality and DelayedWETH delay) introduced in ethereum-optimism/optimism#23215 and ethereum-optimism/optimism#23215

The standard ranges for these delays are widened to the configured bounds and a range is added for the DelayedWETH delay. The staging compliance report now shows the delays of a new chain against those ranges, and a new check groups every registered chain by `ETHLockbox` and asserts that the delays are within range and identical across chains sharing a lockbox, including those in the interop set.

## Changes

- `validation`: `proof_maturity_delay_seconds` is `[86400, 604800]`, `dispute_game_finality_delay_seconds` is `[43200, 302400]`, and a new `[delayed_weth] delay_seconds = [43200, 604800]` table and `DelayedWETHParams` struct are added. The bounds match `op-deployer`'s `standard` package and `StandardValidatorUtils.sol`. `Range.WithinRange`, previously unused, get a test.
- `ops/internal/report`: `ScanL1` reads the three delays via a new `ScanReviewPeriod` and the comment template renders a "Review Period Delays" block. Both delays are read from the OptimismPortal, which keeps a legacy `disputeGameFinalityDelaySeconds()` forwarding to the AnchorStateRegistry on every release, so no release gating is needed. `checkmarkRangeUint64` now delegates to `Range.WithinRange` instead of reimplementing it.
- `ops/internal/manage`: `ReviewPeriodChecker` reads the delays of every chain with an `EthLockboxProxy` over the superchain's L1 RPC and fails on out-of-range values or on any difference between chains sharing a lockbox. All three delays are compared, matching `OPContractsManagerMigrator._validateSharedDelays`. The DelayedWETH is resolved from `SystemConfig.delayedWETH()` because `addresses.json` has no `DelayedWETHProxy` for permissioned-only chains.
- `ops/cmd/check_review_period_delays`, a `just check-review-period-delays` recipe, a `check-review-period-delays` CircleCI job on PRs and a copy in the daily scheduled workflow, since delays change through superchain-ops tasks rather than registry PRs.

## Notes

- Today all 8 lockbox chains are on distinct lockboxes with the default delays, so the equality rule is vacuous until interop sets share a lockbox. Verified against the live registry.
- The lockbox check is also run by `TestReviewPeriodChecker_actual` inside the existing `go-lint-test-ops` job, so the dedicated CI job only adds the daily run.

Closes [#812](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/812)

topPRs.title: ops: keep genesis files as opaque JSON
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #1382 (needs its monorepo bump for `op-core/genesis`).

The registry no longer uses op-geth's genesis types: it keeps genesis files as opaque JSON, validates them with op-core, and writes op-deployer's genesis as is. Decoding through `core.Genesis` keeps only the fields the linked geth knows, and upstream go-ethereum's chain config has no OP fields (`optimism`, `regolithTime`…`jovianTime`, `bedrockBlock`), so on upstream geth these would be dropped silently from every genesis the registry publishes.

- `ReadGenesis`/`WriteGenesis` (used by `sync_staging`) keep the genesis JSON byte for byte. `TestGenesisRoundTrip` round-trips every file under `superchain/extra/genesis` and checks the bytes are unchanged; some files are pretty-printed, so a decode and re-encode would not keep them.
- `ValidateGenesisIntegrity` builds an `op-core/params.ChainConfig` from the chain's TOML and compares `op-core/genesis.ToBlock().Hash()` instead of hand-building an op-geth config. Every chain `check_genesis_integrity` checks still matches its hash. op-core rejects `stateHash`, which only the legacy-migrated chains the check already skips use.
- `create_config` writes `op-deployer inspect genesis` output compacted, which keeps its key order (go-ethereum's `core.Genesis` order). This drops `opaqueToGenesis` and its losslessness check. Unlike before, an old op-deployer's `terminalTotalDifficultyPassed` is kept and op-geth's `"slotNumber":null` is no longer added.

topPRs.title: ops: bump monorepo to develop and switch to op-service/log
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Bumps `ops` to monorepo develop at ethereum-optimism/optimism@fbfb3587c9 (ethereum-optimism/optimism#23527) and op-geth to `v1.101702.4-rc.1`, the version that commit pins.

- ethereum-optimism/optimism#23527 moved op-fetcher's library: the `fetch/script` types are now in `op-fetcher/chaininfo` (`ChainConfig` → `Config`, `CreateChainConfig(out)` → `out.Config()`), with the same JSON shape. op-fetcher now reads chain info with `eth_call`s instead of a forge script. A full `codegen` run against public L1 RPCs gives the same output on this branch as on `main`.
- `fetch.NewFetcher` now takes `op-service/log`'s `Logger`, so `ops` logs through `op-service/log` instead of `go-ethereum/log`.
- The `validation` requirement in `ops/go.mod` moves up to the version the monorepo requires. `ops/go.work` still resolves it to the local module.

topPRs.title: ops: read superchain.toml from disk for the standard state
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
`ops` took the standard op-deployer state's SuperchainConfig address from op-geth's `superchain` package, which embeds a copy of this registry's own configs. It now reads `superchain/configs/{mainnet,sepolia}/superchain.toml` from the repo. To find it, the state mergers, `OpDeployer` and the staging report now take the repo root.

This uses the registry's current data instead of a stale copy. The pinned op-geth embeds a snapshot of this repo from June. A change to a network's `superchain_config_addr` used to take effect only after a new op-geth snapshot and an op-geth bump. Now it applies in the same PR, and a network that isn't in the snapshot works too. Today the values are the same for both networks, and `TestMergeState`'s golden output covers sepolia.

This was the only op-geth-only package `ops` imported.

Conflicts with #1382 in the `deployer_test.go` imports only.

topPRs.title: Add kona-client v1.8.1-rc.1 and v1.8.1 prestates
topPRs.author: pauldowman
topPRs.body:
Adds the reproducible `cannon64-kona` and `cannon64-kona-interop` prestates for kona-client v1.8.1-rc.1 and v1.8.1, the v1.8 backport release for the eMudhra CA distrust (ethereum-optimism/optimism#23566, ethereum-optimism/optimism#23567) and the go1.26.10 toolchain bump (ethereum-optimism/optimism#23546).

- Both tags point at the same commit (`739d6110ca`), so the two versions carry the same hashes. They were built with `just reproducible-kona-prestate` at that commit.
- The hashes are identical to v1.8.0, because the backport only changes the images' trust store and toolchain, not the kona-client program.
- Both hashes are published in the prestate bucket.
